discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and moire quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle of about 1.1 degrees, the interlayer coupling in bilayer graphene produces nearly flat electronic bands, so that interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity proximate to them, with a phase diagram strikingly reminiscent of the cuprates. The work created a new field: moire materials as tunable platforms where carrier density, bandwidth and topology are controlled by gates and twist angle. It has since yielded orbital ferromagnetism, quantum anomalous Hall states, nematic and intertwined orders, and fractional Chern insulators without magnetic field. For the first time, strongly correlated electron physics can be explored systematically, in situ, within a single device. Few contributions in the past two decades have so profoundly reshaped how our community approaches the problem of strong correlations and high-temperature superconductivity.
